My question to you was this: If the Autonomous Region of Krajina had guaranteed that the Muslims would enjoy all of their rights as citizens, then you would not have been opposed; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know that. I cannot give you an answer to something that would happen if something else were to happen.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you were asked by the Prosecutor, and you sat here -- not here, in another courtroom, under oath, and told these Judges that the reason you were opposed to joining the Autonomous Region of Krajina was that it did not guarantee that Muslims would enjoy all of their rights as citizens. Now, that's what you said to these Judges, and doesn't that mean that if it had guaranteed all of those rights, you would not have opposed it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Probably not, had Croatia remained within Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, when you were asked that question last week, you didn't say anything about Croatia remaining in Yugoslavia, did you? You just said your problem was that it didn't guarantee that Muslims would enjoy the rights as citizens.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is correct, but I had the general situation in mind in relation to the settlement of the status of the former Yugoslavia, because this is the reason why -- this status is the reason why war broke out in the area of the former Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you may have had it in mind, sir, but you didn't tell these Judges that, did you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Nobody asked me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Really. Question: "You as a Muslim in a municipality that was taken into this new separatist commune, how was that, did you think, going to affect you personally as a Muslim, if at all?" Answer: "This new para-state did not guarantee that the Muslims would enjoy all of their rights as citizens." You were definitely asked, and that was the answer you gave, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: This is becoming argument. Your Honours saw the question and heard the answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I will.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at Exhibit P80, please. Sir, what you have before you now is the Statute of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, and I want to direct your attention to Article 4 thereof. And it reads as follows, does it not: "In carrying out work from the jurisdiction of the Autonomous Region of Krajina, all nations and nationalities in the Autonomous Region of Krajina shall be equal in their rights and duties, without distinction as to race, sex, birth, language, nationality, religion, political or other beliefs, education, social background, wealth, or any other personal qualities." Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So the constitution of the Autonomous Region of Krajina did in fact guarantee your rights as citizens, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is possible. I was not familiar with the Statute.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How on earth could you have been so opposed to it if you didn't even know what it said?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We could because we saw what happened in the Republic of Croatia with the Krajinas, that this caused the war, and the idea was for Serbs to join together and to form -- to join Serbia and to form Greater Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, I want to go back to your answer on page 41 to that same question we've been talking about. I now want to refer to the first part of your answer. The question, I'll remind you again, was: "You, as a Muslim in a municipality that was taken into this new separatist commune, how was that, did you think, going to affect you personally as a Muslim, if at all?" Your answer was this, sir: "Since a referendum of the Serbian people was held and that they came out in favour of staying within Yugoslavia," and then you went on to say: "This new para-state did not guarantee that the Muslims would enjoy all their rights ..." That's another answer you just kind of made up because you thought it sounded good, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I didn't make anything up. A referendum was held, and all Serbs came out in favour of remaining within the state of Yugoslavia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes, but you were being asked why you were opposed to joining the Autonomous Region of Krajina, which was created in September of 1991 and which was a proposal that was made within Kljuc in September of 1991, and you said one of those reasons that you didn't want to join it was because of the referendum of the Serb people which was held in November of 1991, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as the dates are concerned, it was a long time ago, so I cannot say all the dates with precision. But what I said is true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you were just making up reasons that sounded good, without regard to the facts, just to try to make the Judges feel like you were telling them something important.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You can leave the last part out, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I want to -- page 48 of your testimony, sir, you were talking about -- you were asked this question, line 20. In essence, the question was: "Were you still able before May to receive broadcasts from Sarajevo?" And your answer was this: "As far as broadcasts are concerned, sometime in April we were no longer able to receive Sarajevo as far as the media were concerned."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was your answer; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's right. As far as television and newspapers are concerned, we did not have the possibility of watching or reading the papers from ...

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'm only talking about television. I'm not talking about papers. It's your testimony that you couldn't get television from Sarajevo; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I said both television, but also the press. We were not able to buy papers at news stands.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you be shown document P898, please. Sir, we've -- the Judges have seen this document before. What I want to do is direct your attention to paragraph 3, "situation in the territory," and very near the end of that paragraph there is -- there is a paragraph which begins with the language: "The TV repeater on the Osljak relay station." Let me know when you find that.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I've found it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says: "The TV repeater on the Osljak relay station in the village of Ramici was sabotaged, and as a result there is no TV signal reception in the Kljuc area. The sabotage was carried out by Muslim extremists in response to the capture of the transmitter on Mount Vlasic. Do you know anything about this? Do you know if that's true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I've heard about this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know if it's true? Do you know if that's the case, that the repeater was damaged by Muslim extremists?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I heard that a man from Ramici had been arrested, but I did not -- I was not familiar with any of the details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you tell us how it was, in view of what you have said about being able to watch Sarajevo television -- well, first of all, you know who Muhamed Filipovic was, the brother of Omer, don't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How is it that Muhamed Filipovic was able to watch the first programme of Sarajevo television --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I object to that question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- up until the time he was arrested?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: On what basis?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: On the basis that it maybe testimony of another witness but pure comment. He can't put to him what Muhamed Filipovic says he was able to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I certainly can.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No, you can't.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It's improper questioning, Your Honour, to say how is it to a witness, that Mr. Filipovic says that he was able to watch television. How is that a proper question? What is the witness supposed to say?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: The witness is supposed to explain how, according to him, he couldn't watch -- follow Sarajevo TV, while it's being put to him that others living in the same village could.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what's being put to him is what the testimony of another witness may or may not have been. What is this witness supposed to say? Mr. Filipovic must have been wrong. It's pure comment. It's comment, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I don't see it that way, Ms. Korner.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how it is that Mr. Filipovic was able to watch the Sarajevo programme up until his arrest?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: According to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: According to him, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'd like a quotation, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'd like the exact quotation of what Mr. Filipovic is alleged to have said.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're right.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: And Your Honour, I maintain the objection, because in my view that's an improbable question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, among other things, it comes under Ms. Korner's insistence that I always put my case to the witness and I'm doing that.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, the way to put a case is not by saying what a witness may or may not have said. You can put a fact, but you cannot put it in the form of this is what another witness may have said, because what you're inviting this witness to do is to comment. That is standard practice.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm on page 10044, cross-examined by Mr. Zecevic: "In any case, you were able to watch Sarajevo television first channel?" Answer: "While I was at home until I was imprisoned, I could watch it, but there was some interference and there was often an Austrian channel interfering." "But you watched Sarajevo first channel, the first programme with Sarajevo television you watched?" Answer: "When I was at home, when there was no interference with the Austrian programme, yes."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: And my question to you: Could you watch Sarajevo TV, first channel at any time prior to your arrest but proximate to your arrest?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] From about mid-April until the end of May, you couldn't watch the programme, because the repeater on Mount Kozara had been turned towards Belgrade, and the only programme you could follow was that the TV Belgrade and that of TV Banja Luka. So no, I couldn't. Whether anyone else could follow that programme, I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Next question, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony last week, page 48, line 6, Ms. Korner was asking you about the positioning of the Knin Corps at Laniste and a vote that was taken in favour of that. And then you were asked how it made you feel, as Bosniaks. And your answer, sir, on line 6 was this: "We felt unsafe, as earlier we had seen groups arriving, groups of volunteers from the front in Croatia, who were not under anybody's control." What do you mean, they were not under anybody's control?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, an indication of them being under no one's control was what they did around the town of Kljuc and the other villages. They fired shots from firearms on a daily basis, and that meant that they were under no one's control, because had they been under someone's control, they probably wouldn't have done anything like that. Their aim was to intimidate people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In your testimony at page 50, you were talking about attempts by individuals among the Muslim population to procure weapons because of the security situation. You indicated that you personally had a pistol. Then you were asked this question: "And when you say that there were attempts by individuals to procure weapons, what do you mean by that?" Answer: "The very closeness of the front in Croatia and the opening of a front at Kupres, and especially the return of combatants from those fronts instilled fear and jeopardised the security, and people fearing this armed themselves by purchasing weapons from certain people who came to the area." Do you recall that answer?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And isn't it the case that the very closeness of the front in Croatia and the attitude of the Muslim people regarding participating in what was going on in Croatia instilled fear in the Serb population of Kljuc, based upon their memories of what happened during World War II and their fears of a rebirth of a Muslim/Croat coalition? Isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not true, because there was no coalition on our part. As far as war was concerned, the Bosniaks simply wanted no part in it, in the war in Croatia, on the Croatian front.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, what in fact you said was you weren't going to fight against Croats, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: We had no intention of fighting anyone, including Croats, because people from the municipal area did go to the front, and they fought Croats there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Kljuc -- when do you want to break, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Half past -- [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I'm way off.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In Kljuc, the Muslims formed the Patriotic League, did they not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not true. What did happen is that the TO was formed, a TO unit was formed by the commander of the army staff of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So there was no Patriotic League operating in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were not part of any Patriotic League operating in Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I was only a member of the staff for political relations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That was the Crisis Staff, was it not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was a TO staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There was also a Crisis Staff formed, though, was there not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: There should have been one, but this never materialised, for the simple reason that it wasn't possible.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were asked -- page 51 of the transcript, line 23, you were asked: "Did you, the Bosniaks, form any kind of a Crisis Staff?" Answer: "Yes." Question: "At what stage?" Answer: "There was an attempt to form such a staff in mid-May." Question: "And who was the head of the staff?" Answer: "In the -- at first it should have been Mr. Filipovic." So your answer is that there was an attempt to do this in mid-May, I take it. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Sefer Halilovic is?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he headed an organisation called the Patriotic League?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I wouldn't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I want to read to you from the testimony of Muhamed Filipovic and ask you whether this is true or not, page 9372, on questioning by Ms. Korner?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I object. All he's being asked to do is comment on another witness's testimony. It's an improper form of questioning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Here you are right, Ms. Korner. Put the question what facts you want him to confirm or deny.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'll do that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: During Mr. Filipovic's direct testimony, sir --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Put the fact.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: It is perfectly -- Mr. Ackerman is an experienced enough counsel merely to put a fact that he wishes the witness to agree or disagree with. It is unnecessary to state that it comes from any other witness's testimony. It is a form of speech-making and comment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In the other instance, I allowed the question, Mr. Ackerman, because the position was that you were putting to the witness that two persons in the same city, in the same location, could possibly not be receiving the same TV. Now it's different. Now you're going to put a fact, just put that fact, without reference to any particular witness. And then if it is necessary to refer to the witness, I will let you do it, but not in the first place.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I understand, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, wasn't it a fact that in the Kljuc municipality, the Patriotic League of the Kljuc municipality was created, that in 1991 it had 50 members, that later on the number of members escalated to somewhere around 100 to 150, and that it was different from the Territorial Defence? Is that true?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: In other words, Mr. Egrlic, it's being put to you that in the Kljuc municipality there was indeed a Patriotic League which was set up in 1991, initially having 50 members, later increasing to around 100 to 150, and that this was an entity which was substantially different from what you have referred to as the Territorial Defence. If you are aware of this, if you agree with this, just say yes; if you don't agree with it, just say no. We're talking of the municipality and not the town.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He doesn't agree, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if Mr. Filipovic testified that that was the case, you disagree with his testimony?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: What do you mean? Yes or no? You disagree or you don't disagree?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't agree that there was a Patriotic League. What I'm saying is that only Territorial Defence existed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Whoever would maintain that there was a Patriotic League, you wouldn't agree with him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that there was a Crisis Staff that was formed during the second half of 1991 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's testified about that already.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- And that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's testified about that, and you've just asked him a couple of questions. You were actually reading from his own testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: He said it was formed in May of 1992 and they could never meet. It's a different question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, this is a different one.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Oh, I see. Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you agree that there was a Crisis Staff formed during the second half of 1991, of which you were a member?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And so I take it that if Muhamed Filipovic --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: No. I'm sorry, Your Honour. This has got to stop. He's deliberately flouting Your Honour's ruling.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. Exactly. You're right, Ms. Korner. I will not let you --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I take the gravest possible exception. It's not the first time it has happened. It's not a proper way to cross-examine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes. She is right.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I don't know what I'm doing wrong.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Because you're putting to the witness the name of another witness, basically to show him that some other witness has stated exactly the opposite of what he is stating, when you don't need to reveal the name of the other witness. You just say: I put it to you that there have been other witnesses that have -- that have stated that there was a Crisis Staff. Do you agree or you don't agree? And he's already told you that he doesn't agree that there was a Crisis Staff set up in the second half of 1991. So the matter stands there. I mean, one witness may have stated the opposite. He's stating exactly the opposite.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's also the objection of Ms. Korner is being sustained for another reason, that it's not right that you present the witness with information leading him to understand that another witness also coming from the political arena gives a completely different story to his with regard to some details at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to look at Exhibit P1010, 1010, please. While we're waiting for that, sir, it was your position with regard to the Crisis Staff that because it wasn't formed until May and there were roadblocks in May, that you were never able to meet; correct? I'm sorry. Did you hear my question just now?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I hope so.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, the document you have before you, sir, is a report, and I'm only interested in having you look at the first paragraph of that, which talks about the Crisis Staff of the SDS in Kljuc, which was established on 23 December 1991 and then became the Crisis Staff of the Kljuc Municipal Assembly on 14 May 1992. Do you agree with those dates?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Well, probably, yes, but I don't know the dates precisely, so I can't say anything concerning the dates.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm finished with that document now.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I'm sorry. Just so it's clear. I understood that Mr. Egrlic was talking about the Bosniak Crisis Staff, and that's what he was being asked about, and this document refers to the SDS Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes. It was a totally different question. I was asking about the SDS Crisis Staff and the municipal Crisis Staff formed by the Serbian people, on a completely different tack.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is a report of the Crisis Staff of the SDS.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Sir, I'm finished with that document. You may give it back.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Page 53 of last week's transcript, you were asked if you had heard about a Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, and you said that you did. You were asked when you first heard of that Crisis Staff, and you said you heard about it for the first time sometime in April of 1992. And you said that the head of that Crisis Staff, you heard, was Mr. Brdjanin. Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you recall who it was you heard that from, that there was such a Crisis Staff and that Mr. Brdjanin was the head of it, in April of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't know exactly who I heard this from, but I did hear it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that the Crisis Staff that Mr. Brdjanin was the president of was not even formed until May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I don't know the date of the establishment of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you told the Judges that you heard about it in April and that Mr. Brdjanin was the president, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And will you concede that couldn't have been true if that Crisis Staff wasn't started until May of 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: As far as the date is concerned, it's very difficult now, after ten years, to be clear about the dates when certain things were happening.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were then asked this question: "Were you aware of any connections before your arrest at the end of May between that Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, headed by Mr. Brdjanin, and the Crisis Staff in Kljuc, the SDS Crisis Staff?" Do you remember that question?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And your answer was: "I didn't hear anything in particular from the document which I received by accident except from the document I received by accident." You're talking about that telex document, aren't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you to be shown a couple of documents: P168 and again P22. Now, sir, I show you P168 first just to give you an assurance that the Autonomous Region of Krajina's Crisis Staff or war staff was created by Nikola Erceg on 5th May 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I see that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, this document that you say showed a connection between the Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, headed by Mr. Brdjanin, and the Crisis Staff in Kljuc, this document P22, is dated 29 October 1991, six months before there was any Crisis Staff headed by Mr. Brdjanin; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It is correct, but this document, as far as the municipal Crisis Staff is concerned, was implemented fully, which means that this Crisis Staff accepted it as its own.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We just spent a lot of time, an hour or so ago, going through that document, and you told us you didn't even know if large parts of it had been implemented, and now you're saying it was implemented fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He's already explained that before, Mr. Ackerman. Let's move to the next question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you told the Judges that this fax that you got showed a connection between the Crisis Staff in Banja Luka, headed by Mr. Brdjanin, and the Crisis Staff in Kljuc, that was another one of those things you just made up, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That is not true. This document was a task for the Kljuc SDS, a task that was to be implemented.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But it doesn't come from any ARK Crisis Staff headed by Mr. Brdjanin, does it, because there wasn't one then?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: But this document was adopted as the objective, and the SDS Crisis Staff in Kljuc was implementing it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm going to go to something different now. In your testimony, on page 55 --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, actually, this is kind of a long --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll stop here.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: -- process here. Maybe it's a good idea to break now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: We'll break for 25 minutes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Now, let me say, in connection with when I might finish, I can tell you that I'm on page 7 of 10 pages of notes, which will become about 12 pages of notes. I think maybe about another hour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: If it's another hour, I don't --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think I've got some re-examination, so I think the witness will have to come back briefly tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. Thank you. So 25 minutes, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, during your testimony last week, page 55, line 11, you were asked the following question: "Do you remember hearing any announcement on the radio or on television or elsewhere about weapons having to be surrendered?" Answer: "I heard this announcement on Radio Kljuc." Question: "And who was being ordered to surrender their weapons?" Answer: "The announcement applied to Bosniaks." I'd like you first to look at Exhibit P922. And I'd like you to look at this, sir. It's from Radio Kljuc. I want to know if this is the announcement that you were referring to when you gave that answer.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm seeing this for the first time. This pertains to the late Mr. Omer Filipovic. He was arrested on the 28th of May, in the morning hours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember the question that I asked you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes. I responded that I don't know this announcement. There was a different announcement on Radio Kljuc about handing over weapons.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. So this is not the one you were referring to. This is a different announcement about --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He couldn't be referring to it, because he's saying this is the first time he has come across it, so he couldn't have referred to it in his testimony.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Well, Your Honour, it would be one thing to come across the written form and another to hear it on the radio. My question was: Is this what he heard on the radio? And he says no, that this isn't it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Exactly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Would you look, then, at P196, sir. Now, this document, sir, comes from the Kljuc municipality Crisis Staff, and I'll refer you to paragraph 1. It says: "Citizens who are in possession of weapons procured illegally are here asked to surrender them between 1200 and 1400 hours today at the Kljuc Public Security Station or the nearest police station point." Might it have been a report of this decision of the Crisis Staff that you heard on the radio?

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: I'm sorry, Your Honour. I've lost -- where is that part?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It's paragraph 1: "Citizens who are in possession of weapons ..."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: "... procured illegally are here asked to surrender them between 1200 hours and 1400 hours today at the Kljuc Public Security Station."

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't think that's P196.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Sorry. It's got 196 on the --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm sorry.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Might it be the case that it is the radio report of this order was what you heard on the radio about weapons surrender?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: For the record, just before he answers, may I just point out that according to the transcript, first time you referred this document to be produced it was referred to in the transcript as P196, and it should be 916.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. My mistake, obviously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right, sir. Can you answer the question?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm not familiar with this document. It bears the date the 28th of May. I had heard something around the 15th about the ultimatum being set.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Then could you please be shown P167. And this is a decision that comes from the Secretariat for National Defence, signed by Colonel Sajic, and paragraph -- it's paragraph 5 of that decision that I'm interested in having you look at. It's dated 4 May of 1992. And that paragraph reads: "All paramilitary formations and individuals in possession of illegal weapons and ammunition are asked to surrender those weapons and ammunition immediately, or not later than 1500 hours on 11 May 1992, to the municipal TO headquarters or the nearest public security station. Once this deadline has expired, the responsible bodies shall carry out the search and confiscation of weapons and ammunition and shall apply the most appropriate sanctions." Do you think it might have been a report about this decision that you heard on Radio Kljuc?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. It was a Crisis Staff decision. This is a decision, as far as I can see, by the military leadership of the then Republika Srpska, and I heard on Radio Kljuc the decision by the Crisis Staff of the municipality of Kljuc, the Serb Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The government of Republika Srpska, in that paragraph, was ordering that all persons illegally in possession of weapons should surrender them, not just Bosniaks; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This pertains only to Bosniaks, because I didn't hear anywhere that they went to take weapons by force from the Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Show me in paragraph 5 where it's limited to Bosniaks. What language in paragraph 5 says it's limited to Bosniaks? Can you see it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about what happened and not what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It doesn't say that in paragraph 5, does it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So if the people in Kljuc did something different, they were violating this order, weren't they, this decision?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: They were not violating it, because this is a decision by the then illegal Republika Srpska of the Bosnia and Herzegovina at that time. Bosnia and Herzegovina was an internationally recognised state, without Republika Srpska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, was the illegal Serbian Crisis Staff in Kljuc violating the order of the illegal Republika Srpska government by confiscating weapons only from Bosniaks? That was my question. We can argue all day about what was legal and illegal, and I'm not going to do that with you.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: What is the question?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm not going to ask it. I'll withdraw it. I'm through with all those documents now. During your testimony last week, page 56, line 2, you were asked this question: "Did there come a time when you did hand over your weapon?" Answer: "I handed over my weapon on the 27th of May."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: He corrected that eventually, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question is: Why did you say that to the Judges?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was simply a confusion about the dates. It wasn't the 27th, but it was the 28th. I said that that happened after my self-inflicted injury.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are two facts in that answer. The first one is: I handed over my weapon. The second is that it was on the 27th of May. Both of them are wrong, aren't they?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Let him make it clear. What's being suggested to you is that you made two mistakes in one statement, namely, when you said that you surrendered the weapon on the 27th, but in reality, later on you correct yourself and said that you had surrendered it on the 28th. And secondly, that while you still say that you surrendered it, in real fact you later also explained that it was Omer Filipovic that surrendered it after you had inflicted the -- you had wounded yourself accidentally. So what's being asked of you is to explain why in one simple sentence you made two mistakes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It was simply a slip. On the 28th of May, I injured myself, in the morning, and the gun, the pistol, remained at the place where I injured myself. And this pistol was then handed over by Omer Filipovic. I don't know on what day.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke in your testimony about being questioned, interrogated, in Stara Gradiska, and later at Manjaca, by a captain who you said was called Zenga. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the origin and the meaning of the name Zenga?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's an abbreviation for Zbor Narodne Garde, National Guards Corps.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Of Croatia; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, Croatia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And was this captain a Croat?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The captain was a Serb. I don't know what he was, but I assume that he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The name Zenga might indicate that he was not a Serb but a Croat, though, mightn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It would not necessarily indicate that, because the other guards also used nicknames to shield themselves. There was a guard whose nickname was Fadil, but he was a Serb.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Once you got to Manjaca, you talked about the guards there being police. Were they regular police or were they military police, or do you not know?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I think it was the military police.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Why do you think so?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because they had camouflage uniforms, just like the soldiers.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'd like you now to look at P1113. Now, you told us last week that this was a statement that was created as a result of interrogations that were going on of you in Manjaca; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the person who was questioning you you said was making notes during the course of the questioning. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the first page, you said that everything there was true and correct until we got down to a sentence that began and continued as follows: "Those employed in the Kljuc TO and those from the Kljuc SJB who did not sign the declaration of loyalty to the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina were supposed to join the staff command. He," and I assume that's you, "emphasised that he personally did not talk to these people, but assumed that they would probably have consented in order to secure the subsistence of their families, since they had no jobs." When asked who replaced Suad Mesic as the person responsible for medical matters in the Bosanski Kljuc TO staff, he replied that it was most likely to be Dr. Emir Kapetanovic." Now, I think you told us that you didn't say any of those things and that those things were not true. Am I right about that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The question is: The things that I just read out to you, I think you told us yesterday that you did not say those things and that those things were not true.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It's true that I said that a Crisis Staff was formed and that the commander of the Crisis Staff of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina appointed the late Omer Filipovic as the commander of the Kljuc TO.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That's not -- you're not answering the question. Last Friday, Ms. Korner handed you this document, which purportedly is a statement that was made by you, following a series of questions at the Kljuc police station. Ms. Korner went through that document, or substantial parts of that document, paragraph by paragraph, and you were asked at the time two questions. This document says the following, that you said the following. Did you actually state this to the interrogator? And if you did, was it true or not? And as far as this particular paragraph that was read out to you by Mr. Ackerman is concerned, it's being put to you that on Friday you said that you never made this part of the statement to the investigator or to the interviewer and that in any case it wasn't true, what's contained in there is not true. And the same question, more or less, is being repeated now at this time from Mr. Ackerman. Do you confirm your position?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I confirm it and I explain it by saying that I said who was appointed as the commander of the TO staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I think we're having a monumental failure of communication here. Do you see the sentence that begins with: "Those employed in the Kljuc TO and those from the Kljuc SJB ..." Do you see that? It's up above the Crisis Staff part that you're referring to.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I found it. I did not state that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your position, then, that whoever it was that prepared this note up until that point had accurately reported what you had said and then just added this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I think that that is correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if we go down to: "The Crisis Staff comprised Muhamed Filipovic as leader, Asim Egrlic; Omer Filipovic, commissar; Ihsan Zukanovic, training; Suad Mesic, health care; Ibrahim Egrlic, security; Hamed Brkovic, courier; and Kemo Bender, and was disbanded immediately before the formation of the Bosanski Kljuc TO." I think you told us that that bit was not true and that you didn't say it. Am I correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I've said that several times, that the Crisis Staff was to have been formed, but it was basically never formed, and that this is not correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But wasn't it true that that Crisis Staff which you say was never formed was to have Muhamed Filipovic as leader and you and these other people as members?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: What I said was that the Crisis Staff -- what is understood by the Crisis Staff, is that it was to be composed of people who had been legally elected to certain offices and who should have an official duty to form part of the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: If you go, then, sir, after the part referring to the TO, there's just a sentence sitting all by itself. It says: "He stated that the village guards grew into platoons and companies." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it your position that there never was, within the Kljuc municipality, a platoon or a company of the Muslim TO?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Up until the time that I was still there, no, there was nothing. There were guards.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, if you look at the next paragraph, it speaks of you going to Zagreb. You in fact did go to Zagreb, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when was that?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I can't remember the date exactly, but it may have been in April 1992.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And out of that trip, whether directly or indirectly, you in fact acquired weapons, didn't you?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's what it says here, but that's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know what a Heckler is?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I want to make sure that this is being correctly interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: H-e-c-k-l-e-r.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I'm not in a position to know whether it's being correctly interpreted.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It may not be.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In terms of a firearm, do you know of a firearm called a Heckler?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, I know nothing about such a firearm.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about a firearm called a Zagi?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I've heard about that weapon, but I don't know what it looks like.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that you had two of these, one of which you gave to Omer Filipovic and one of which you kept yourself?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You mean the Zagi?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It is true that I had a pistol, and I did have permission to be in possession of that pistol.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you have two pistols, one of which you gave to Omer Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I only had one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What was it you had two of in terms of weapons, one of which you gave to Omer Filipovic?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: The only thing I had was one pistol, and I didn't give it to anyone. It remained with Omer Filipovic after I was wounded, and then afterwards he handed it over.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did you ever serve in the Yugoslav army?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And didn't you learn while you were serving in the Yugoslav army what a weapon called a Heckler was?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. I had only signed for an M-48 rifle while I was in Mostar, during my military service.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I must put to you the following proposition, sir: I put to you that you had two Hecklers, one of which you gave to Omer Filipovic. Is that true or not true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Down near the bottom of what is the second page in English, after -- there's a list of three persons: Omer Filipovic, Mumin Egrlic and Ibrahim Egrlic. The following paragraph appears: "In response to the question where he was prior to the shooting at the police and the army, he stated that on 26 May 1992 he, attending a meeting held at the cultural centre in Pudin Han." Were you at the cultural centre in Pudin Han on 26 May 1992?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, you've told us that the Crisis Staff couldn't meet because there were travel restrictions and you couldn't travel. How is it you were able to travel to Pudin Han?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I reached Pudin Han when the population from the village in which I live had fled, and I reached Pudin Han through the woods.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Now, other people reached Pudin Han to participate in this meeting: Omer Filipovic, Amir Avdic, Nevzad Djeric, Velid Ticevic, Ale Mujezinovic, Enes Salihovic, Fahrudin Cemal, Enes Sistak and perhaps others. All those people were there at that time, were they not?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That may well have been that most of those people were indeed there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this was basically the executive board of the SDA, wasn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the truth is that you were able to travel and able to have meetings and that you did have several meetings of both the SDA executive board and the TO staff of which you were also a part; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Until the 7th of May, yes, we could have regular meetings, but not after that date, because roads were blocked and there were Serbian checkpoints manned by Serbian police.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sir, I'd like the Prosecutor to supply you with your statement to the Office of the Prosecutor of 13 March 2001, please. In this statement, and it's page 4 of the English version, you're speaking of a document that you had had in your possession that was lost when your home was burned, and what you told the Prosecutor investigator was this: "The document was a fax message. It was signed by Radoslav Brdjanin as president of the Assembly of the Krajina region and it was addressed to all the presidents of municipal Crisis Staff. My office was next to Jovo Banjac. Our two offices were separated by a secretary's office. I don't recall her name. She brought the fax message to me. When I saw the document, I realised that it was not for me. I made a copy of it and then gave the fax message to Banjac." Now, this is the same document we've been talking about earlier, the P22 document, the telex, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you described that document as you could remember two things that came from the document; correct? You say to set up War Presidencies, so replace non-Serb officials. Those were two things you could remember at the time that had been in that document; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I'd like you to now be handed P22. All right, sir. You now have, in addition, this document, P22. What you told the Prosecutor's investigator about this document was this: "Stojan Zupljanin was chief of police for the whole ARK region. I know that Zupljanin reported to Radoslav Brdjanin, who was the head of the civilian authority. Unfortunately, I don't have any evidence to prove this now. Before the war, I had a document that proved that Zupljanin was subordinate to Brdjanin. I left the document at home. My home was the first one to be burnt down during the war, and I lost all my possessions along with that document." Now, sir, show us, please, in this document the proof that Zupljanin was subordinate to Brdjanin.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: You can't tell from this document, but it is a well-known fact that chief of the Security Services Centre cannot be an independent figure. We know that he is subordinate to the civilian authorities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, isn't it true that he's subordinated to the head of MUP?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, because when the Autonomous Region of Bosanska Krajina was proclaimed, all links were severed with the centre in Sarajevo, that is, with the Ministry of the Interior there. He could only be --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That is -- [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is my belief.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you saying that the head of the CSB in Banja Luka would not have been responsible to the head of the Minister of the Interior of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Not Serbian one. He was to answer to the Ministry of the Interior of the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, with headquarters in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: You're talking at cross-purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, we are.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The point is this, sir: When you spoke to the Office of the Prosecutor in 2001, on 13 March, you told the investigator that this document would prove that Zupljanin was subordinate to Brdjanin. Now you say that there's nothing in the document that would prove that; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. The only thing this document contains is a number of tasks to be carried out.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this document doesn't even mention the police, does it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This document was taken over from the central office of the SDS in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'll ask you the question again. This document doesn't even mention the police, does it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, it doesn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And when you told Mr. Inayat of the Prosecutor's office, on 13 March 2001, that this document would prove that Zupljanin was subordinate to Brdjanin, you just made that up, didn't you, because you thought the document had been destroyed and you would never be confronted with it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not correct. I based my allegation on what happened after this document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That isn't what you said to Mr. Inayat. What you said to Mr. Inayat was: "I had a document that proved that Zupljanin was subordinate to Brdjanin." And that was not true, was it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true. Well, the way these decisions were implemented, at least.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at, sir, the first paragraph of that document. It talks about an order of the SDS Sarajevo, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It says that order was made public at a meeting of all the municipal presidents on 26 October 1991, at 1500 hours, in Banja Luka; right?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it was at a meeting that was chaired by Dr. Karadzic.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: I did not attend that meeting. That's what this document says.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And it's likely, is it not, that if it was a meeting of all the municipal presidents, that Jovo Banjac was present?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And that Jovo Banjac would have known about this order of the SDS in Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: He must have known.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. I'm finished with that, sir. I'd like you to look at P1114. You've looked at this earlier today. Ms. Korner was asking you about this document. This is the one that you agreed contained your signature. You recall it; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the very beginning, it says: "During May 1992 I attended a meeting in Sanski Most." And you agreed that you had attended such a meeting.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When was it? When in May was that meeting?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Perhaps between the 2nd and the 5th of May. I can't say precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you met there with leaders, basically, of Bosanski Most municipality, Mr. Kurbegovic and Mr. Karabeg; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And the document says that the meeting had to do with the possibility of cooperation between Sanski Most and Kljuc in the event that it would become necessary, since they border each other; correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This was added. What we discussed was the general situation in the Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You said there was no possibility of cooperation because of the roadblocks and so forth. Is that your position?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you travelled all the way to Sanski Most. I assume other people went with you, at least Omer Filipovic. And you never talked about the possibility of cooperating in the defence of your municipalities? It never came up?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No. I never had an opportunity to discuss that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Kind of made it a wasted trip, didn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: It was not wasted. Our aim was to check the situation in that area, in Sanski Most municipality, and to exchange information on events in the area of Bosnia and Herzegovina, because all communication lines were down and there was no communication to the government in Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you couldn't talk to Sanski Most by telephone?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, we couldn't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Look at the last paragraph of this document, please. You told us this morning this was correct. I just want to make sure that that's your position. It says: "It was already too late to return to my family, so I decided to accept an offer to spend the night with a Amir Pobric. The following day I accidentally wounded myself with a pistol and was taken to hospital after I had first been to the SJB at about 0700 hours. I was taken from the hospital to Gradiska." Correct?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's correct. First I came to the SJB, then to the hospital, and then on to Gradiska.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm through with those documents now, sir. Sir, it's the case, isn't it, that the Bosnian municipality of Kljuc was formed and announced prior to the formation of any Serbian municipality of Kljuc; isn't that true?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not true. There was only an announcement for that municipality to be established, but it was never formed, because there was supposed to be a citizens' referendum, but as there were no conditions for the referendum to be held, the municipality was never formed. So there never was such a thing as Bosanski Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So it's not true that the Assembly of the municipality of Bosanski Kljuc met in Pudin Han?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: No, that's not true. What did happen, on the 26th, part of the -- some of the members of the executive board met there, but Bosanski Kljuc municipality never began to operate.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you look, please, at Exhibit P870. Sir, this document is dated January 30th, 1992. I think it's a radio announcement, and it reports at the very beginning the following: "At yesterday's session of the SDA and MBO, the formation of a new municipality of Bosanski Kljuc was proclaimed, which does not accept the unlawful and unconstitutional decisions of the Municipal Assembly concerning the inclusion of this municipality into the Autonomous Region of the Bosnian Krajina." Now, this doesn't say there was a threat to proclaim the municipality of Bosanski Kljuc; it says that the municipality was proclaimed, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: That's not true. If you try reading further down the passage at the bottom of the page, it says that there would be a referendum on the status of Bosanski Kljuc municipality.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, it also says that "This is the first Muslim municipality in Bosnia and Herzegovina. Its fate depends on the move of the partner, the SDS. If there is no regionalisation on an ethnic basis, then there will be no municipality of Bosanski Kljuc either." In other words, they do what you want, as a minority, then you'll abandon your new municipality of Bosanski Kljuc, kind of a blackmail; right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: It's not an unknown phenomenon in politics, Mr. Ackerman.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Right?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: You're right, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: ASIM EGRLIC
utterances.text: This was a public announcement in which there was an opening to establish Bosanski Kljuc municipality, and it was said that as soon as all the conditions were met, a referendum, a citizens' referendum would be held so the citizens could speak out on the issue. This referendum however never took place, so Bosanski Kljuc municipality never came to be.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: How much longer do you think you'll take, Mr. Ackerman?

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: I'm guessing 30 minutes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: So you will regulate yourself knowing how much you need for re-examination.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, what we can hand to Your Honours now is Mr. Ackerman and I have reached an agreement in respect of how the Prijedor evidence is to be called. Can we just hand Your Honours copies?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honours will notice that there's a strike-through which I will agree to.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honour, I was about to refer to that. Mr. Ackerman drafted, I struck through those words because it relates to something Your Honours said, but -- if Your Honour takes it, it will see, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: I think the witness can leave the courtroom. Usher, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Your Honours, in paragraph 3, you will see an original line was struck through. I think Your Honours said something about testimony relating specifically to Stakic would be struck. Your Honour, of course, our case is that Stakic is a part of the joint enterprise for which Mr. Brdjanin --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: That I understand, but there may be data which are --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: There may be, Your Honour. I simply didn't want to be -- what I think the idea is Mr. Ackerman will show us what he wants redacted and then we'll redact and if there's any disagreement, we'll argue for Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: No. I fully understand the joint enterprise element, but I'm pretty sure also that there will be references and specific allegations relative to Stakic which have nothing to do with the joint --

utterances.speaker: MS. KORNER
utterances.text: Almost none.

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: It was just ambiguous. It was ambiguous as written, Your Honour. Parts of the evidence against Stakic, of course, are admissible in this case, parts are not.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
utterances.text: All right. So we resume tomorrow afternoon at a quarter after 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE AGIUS
